description: Office-style ribbon for Windows Forms, ported to .NET 10 with working out-of-process designer support. A fork of WindowsRibbon (https://github.com/harborsiem/WindowsRibbon) and RibbonWinForms - great work by harborsiem and Jose Menendez Poo. It also builds for .NET 8. Tabs, panels, buttons, combo boxes, item groups, button lists, the orb menu, contexts and the quick access toolbar are all editable in the designer, and no design-time tooling is needed at runtime.
releaseNotes: Deleting an orb entry no longer takes the Windows Forms designer down. The delete went through the designer host with an unchecked transaction commit and read the ribbon's drop-down without checking, so a host that hands back no transaction threw a null reference out of the design surface's mouse handling and the design tools server reported it as a modal error; the transaction is now optional, the entry still leaves its collection when the host path fails, a failure is logged to RibbonLibDesign.log instead of escaping, and the design surface's click guard catches anything left. Same code as 1.0.31 otherwise. README fix: the screenshot under the fork description now loads on nuget.org (it used a relative docs/ribbon.png path, which the package does not contain) and the version badge shows the newest release instead of the newest prerelease. Code is unchanged from 1.0.30. Orb menu fixes from 1.0.29: The design surface draws the orb menu in two panes again - menu items on the left, the recent-items caption and list plus the option buttons on the right - instead of one list, while keeping the content-sized layout, the placeholder captions for entries with no text and a single row when a collection holds the same item more than once. At runtime the drop-down only laid its panes and items out when it already had a window handle, but the call that sizes it (OnOpening) runs before the handle exists, so it opened at its default size with empty panes and items at no position; it now measures through the desktop DC when there is no handle and lays out again when the handle is created. Every orb entry, separators included, still opens the same context menu on left or right click, and Delete removes the entry from its collection. Runtime behaviour is otherwise unchanged.
